caption: I work in a bank and I was still paying off the cheapest debt first out of habit instead of the most expensive one. Anyone else finally check the actual interest rates?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R18 500
p/m salary
Living in Vereeniging
slides.body:
Female, 29
Single, no kids
Job: Bank teller
Net salary: R18 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 1 bed in central Vereeniging, water, refuse
slides.body: I approve other people's home loans all day. Mine is a rented room with damp in the corner.

slides.title: Credit card
slides.includes: 27.75% interest, balance from three Black Fridays ago
slides.body: I work in a bank and I still didn't check the actual rate until this year. It's the most expensive thing I own.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: Taken out to be a bridesmaid at a friend's wedding
slides.body: Eleven months left. I remember the dress. I don't remember enjoying the day as much as it's costing me.

slides.title: Store account
slides.includes: Furniture account, two years still to run
slides.body: The lowest interest rate of everything I owe, and I'd been paying it off first out of pure habit.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, plus the days I'm too tired after a shift to cook
slides.body: Nothing dramatic here. Just the one line that never goes down no matter what else does.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Transport, medical aid, funeral policy, stokvel, airtime & data
slides.body: Five small debits that leave before I've made a single decision about them.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R18 500. I move money for a living and it still takes me a full evening to work out where mine went.

slides.title: I stopped paying off the wrong debt first
slides.body:
Beyond Horizon compared avalanche against snowball on what I owe and showed me the credit card was costing more than the loan and the store account combined.

No bank login needed.
